title: Car Rental Rate Classes: Where the Supplier Cannot Provide the Vehicle Booked
content:
Where the supplier advises that the booked vehicle class is not available, the renter is given the nearest available class at no additional charge, and a class above the one booked never carries an upcharge. Where no vehicle at all is available the rental is cancelled free of charge on every rate class and any prepayment is returned in full. A renter who declines a substitute vehicle is treated as cancelling free of charge and not as a no-show. The included mileage, the protection products and the fuel arrangement follow the rate class booked and not the substitute vehicle actually provided. Several notices about the same rental are not added together; the last notice standing before collection decides what is owed. A notice withdrawn by the supplier before collection gives rise to no concession at all.

**The basis of substitution.** The substitute offered is the nearest available class at or above the class booked. A class above the one booked carries no upcharge, so the renter pays what the rental on the Car Rental Rate Classes already provided for and no more.

**The three outcomes a notice can produce.**

| What the supplier advises | What follows |
|---|---|
| The booked vehicle class is not available | The nearest available class at or above it, at no additional charge |
| No vehicle at all is available | The rental is cancelled free of charge on every rate class, and any prepayment is returned in full |
| The notice is withdrawn before collection | No concession at all arises from it |

**A renter who says no to the substitute.** They stand as cancelling free of charge, and not as a renter who failed to collect.

**What the substitute vehicle does not change.** The included mileage, the protection products and the fuel arrangement of the rental follow the rate class booked. The substitute vehicle actually provided does not carry its own terms across.

**Several notices on one rental.** They are not added together. Whichever notice stands last before collection decides what is owed.
